title: The Herdr panel cannot force a fetch, as the dashboard's r does
body:
## Decision

hv's decision 18 of 2026-11-17 (on hv's board, relayed by vc): in the next release, r in the Herdr panel forces a fetch, as the dashboard's r does. ic builds it, in one worktree and one Desk cargo slot.

## Symptom

The panel asks ccusage on its timer, which is never shorter than the usage cache's lifetime (five minutes), and it asks from the cache. Its one command, `ccusage.refresh`, which a confirmed Use sends, also asks from the cache. So the panel has no way to show fresh usage before the cache's lifetime runs out. The dashboard's r fetches every account at once.

## Fix outline

1. r, pressed while the panel holds the keyboard, forces a fetch. The panel takes the keyboard as Herdr's own mods do: a focus handle from `cx.focus_handle()`, tracked on its root. The panel focuses the handle when it opens, when it is clicked, and on the `focus` command, which `pane.go` sends and which Herdr sends again when a popup over the panel closes; mod.json says `"focusable": true`. The panel handles r itself in `on_key_down`, matched on the whole chord, so cmd-r and the other keys pass on. r runs `ccusage which --json --refresh`, which fetches every account at once, though not one in a rate-limit cooldown, as the dashboard's r does; then `predict --json` from the fresh cache. So r needs no line in keys.json. `ccusage.refresh` keeps its name and also forces a fetch, for `run()` or a binding of one's own.
2. While the fetch runs, the panel says "Refreshing accounts". A press while one runs starts no other fetch, and the panel says "Refresh already in progress", the dashboard's words. Every copy of the mod shares one forced fetch, so a press that reaches two shown panels fetches once.
3. The five-minute timer stays as it is, and asks from the cache. The reload after a Use from a card's dialog keeps an unforced path of its own, a command named `ccusage.reload`, because a switch needs no fetch.
4. Docs: README's refresh policy says that a key press forces a fetch (r in the dashboard and in the panel), so the five-minute bound and the count per hour describe the timers. README's Herdr section and RECIPE.md say to click the panel, then press r, with no line in keys.json. The CHANGELOG gets a line under 0.1.11.

## Acceptance

1. With no line in keys.json, r in the panel, once the panel is opened or clicked, runs `which --json --refresh`, then `predict --json`, and the panel shows the answer. Its "as of" moves when the fetch ends, well before the timer's next tick.
2. While the fetch runs, the panel says it is refreshing, and a second press starts no other fetch.
3. The timer, and the reload after a Use, still ask from the cache.
4. `herdr-app check` passes on the installed mod, and README, RECIPE.md and the CHANGELOG say how r works, with no line in keys.json.

## Proof

The mod has no harness that can run it outside Herdr, so nothing here can go red first. `herdr-app check` loads the mod and renders it once: that catches a broken mod, but not a wrong refresh. The proof is `herdr-app check` on the built mod, plus hv's look.

## Progress

- 2026-11-17: the first build (2214b63, green in Desk slot 01M7M8B9RJ4E9T35Z7W6S1NJXC) landed as 4930094 on vc's read. hv's look failed. The mod was installed from that build, and keys.json carried `"mod:ccusage": {"r": "ccusage.refresh"}`, which Herdr listed, but pressing r did nothing, and no forced fetch reached ccusage: by vc's reading, every usage cache still held the time the mod hot-reloaded. Why: the panel never held the keyboard. A Herdr mod takes keys only through a focus handle tracked on its root, as Herdr's own keyboard mods (changes, help, worktree) do. The panel's root had no handle, so a click left the keyboard where it was, and neither a `mod:ccusage` section nor `on_key_down` could reach the panel. ic had taken the guide's line that a mod pane keeps the keyboard when clicked as enough, without checking the shipped mods' code.
- 2026-11-17: the fix, on vc's brief, as fix outline item 1 now reads, was built as 25be3e0. It was green in Desk slot 01M7M9NAJ6B7A00WE74BN7ZB4A, with `herdr-app check` passing on the new main.js and the focusable mod.json, and it landed as 4ae853f on vc's read. hv's second look follows.
